text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers merge their code changes into a shared repository frequently. Each merge automatically triggers a CI pipeline. This pipeline performs an automated build, which compiles the code and packages it. Then, it runs a series of tests, from simple unit checks to complex integration tests. The main goal is catching issues early, almost as soon as they are introduced. If a test fails, the team is alerted immediately, allowing them to fix the problem before it grows. This regular process ensures the software remains stable and reduces the stress of fixing major bugs later.
